summary: Specifies an RTP payload format for Extended Adaptive Multi-Rate Wideband (AMR-WB+) audio. AMR-WB+ extends the AMR-WB speech codec with new frame types for high-quality music as well as speech. A media type registration is included. It is standards-track.

plainLanguage.summary: A sound squeezer that handles both talking and music. This says how to pack the squeezed sound into internet packets.

questions: what is the amr-wb+ rtp clock rate
subtitle: How to pack AMR-WB+ speech and music audio frames into RTP packets, with options for interleaving and redundancy.

tldr.problem: The AMR-WB+ codec adds music-quality audio, stereo and many internal sampling frequencies to the AMR-WB speech codec, and needs a way to travel in RTP packets with frame type, timing and loss resilience intact.
tldr.mechanism: Each RTP payload carries a one-octet header (ISF, TFI, L), a table of contents of frame-type entries, then the audio frames, in either a basic mode or an interleaved mode, with a 72000 Hz timestamp clock.
tldr.outcome: The RFC also registers the audio/AMR-WB+ media type with channels, interleaving and int-delay parameters and maps them to SDP, so streaming applications can negotiate the format.

facts.label: Super-frame
facts.value: 2048 samples per channel, four transport frames

facts.label: Payload header
facts.value: ISF 5 bits, TFI 2 bits, L 1 bit

today: RFC 4352 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It registered the audio/amr-wb+ media subtype with IANA and still defines this payload format as written.

sections.title: What This Payload Format Does
sections.content:
This RFC specifies how to put Extended Adaptive Multi-Rate Wideband (AMR-WB+) audio into the Real-time Transport Protocol, RFC 3550. The format carries mono or stereo audio, can bundle several frames in one payload, and has mechanisms that make the packet stream more robust against loss.

AMR-WB+ extends the AMR-WB speech codec with a wider audio bandwidth for music, native stereo and several internal sampling frequencies. The expected key application is streaming, so the format is octet aligned. A bandwidth-efficient mode like the one in RFC 3267 is left out, because the savings would be very small. Multi-channel transport with separate codec instances is also left out, since stereo is built into the codec. No file format is defined; the RFC points to the ISO-based 3GP format instead.
sections.plainLanguage: This is a packing guide for sound. It says how to put pieces of squeezed music and speech into envelopes so they can be sent across the internet and played in order.

sections.title: The AMR-WB+ Codec and Its Timing
sections.content:
The codec was specified by 3GPP for streaming and messaging in GSM and 3G cellular systems, and the RFC says it also suits other varying transport environments such as the Internet. Encoding works on equally sized super-frames of 2048 samples per channel at the chosen internal sampling frequency (ISF). Each super-frame yields four transport frames of 512 samples, and each transport frame can be used by the decoder on its own if its position in the super-frame is known.

The codec has 13 ISFs from 12.8 to 38.4 kHz. The nominal ISF of 25600 Hz gives an 80 ms super-frame. Frame types 0 to 13 (the AMR-WB types and four fixed extension rates) need no explicit ISF; types 14 to 47 do. Because duration depends on the ISF, a transport frame lasts from 13.33 to 40 ms.

The RTP timestamp clock rate SHALL be 72000 Hz, which makes each frame an integer number of ticks: 960 to 2880, depending only on the ISF. For example, ISF 32000 gives 1152 ticks and ISF 25600 gives 1440 ticks. The encoder may change ISF and frame type during a session, but for frame types 10-13 and 16-47 the change must fall on a super-frame boundary.
sections.plainLanguage: The codec cuts sound into little slices and sends them in groups of four. Each slice can last a different time depending on a setting, so the packet clock ticks in tiny steps that fit every setting evenly.

sections.title: Payload Header and Structure
sections.content:
An RTP payload has a payload header, a table of contents and the audio data. A payload with more than one frame is a compound payload. The RTP marker bit is set to 1 when the first frame is the first of a talkspurt, and the RTP payload type is assigned outside this document.

The one-octet payload header holds ISF (5 bits), TFI (2 bits) and L (1 bit). ISF applies to every frame in the payload and SHALL be 0 when the frames have types 0-13. TFI is the Transport Frame Index, 0 to 3, giving the position of the first frame in the super-frame. L is the long displacement flag used in interleaved mode, and it SHALL be 0 in basic mode.

There are two modes. In basic mode, a payload aggregates consecutive frames. In interleaved mode, it aggregates frames that are not consecutive in time. In both, frame types can be mixed in one payload, but the ISF must be the same for the whole payload, so frames with different ISFs go in separate packets.
sections.plainLanguage: Each envelope has a little label on the front saying how the sound was squeezed and which slice number comes first. The label only needs one byte.

sections.title: The Table of Contents and Timestamps
sections.content:
The table of contents (ToC) lists groups of frames. In basic mode an entry is 16 bits: F (1 bit, 1 if another entry follows), Frame Type (7 bits) and #frames (8 bits). A value of 0 for #frames SHALL NOT be used, and such a packet SHALL be discarded. Entries go in order of increasing RTP timestamp.

In interleaved mode each entry adds a displacement field per frame, giving the distance in frames from the preceding frame. With L=0 these are 4 bits (0 to 15) and a padding nibble is added when the group has an odd number of frames. With L=1 they are 8 bits (0 to 255). The first frame's displacement is meaningless: it is set to zero and ignored.

The first frame's timestamp is the RTP header timestamp. In basic mode, later frames add the frame durations of the preceding ones. For example, with timestamp 12345 and 1152 ticks per frame, the fourth frame is at 12345 + 3 * 1152 = 15801. In interleaved mode, TS(i) = TS(i-1) + (DISi + 1) * frame duration.

Frame type 14 (AUDIO_LOST) and 15 (NO_DATA) carry no audio bytes. An undefined frame type means the whole packet SHALL be discarded. Every audio frame MUST be octet aligned, padded with zeroes if needed.
sections.plainLanguage: Inside the envelope there is a list saying what kinds of sound slices are inside and how many. In the mixed-up mode, the list also says how far apart in time each slice belongs.

sections.title: Surviving Packet Loss
sections.content:
Two mechanisms help. For redundancy, a sliding window lets each frame be sent again in the next packet; the sender needs no negotiation with the receiver, and the cost is bandwidth and receiver delay. All repeated copies MUST have the same frame type, ISF and timestamp, or be NO_DATA. The sender should pick the amount using feedback such as RTCP reports and avoid causing congestion. The RFC points to RFC 2733 and RFC 2198 for generic alternatives.

Interleaving spreads consecutive frames over different packets so a lost packet becomes isolated frame losses that are easier to hide. It adds delay and buffering, and it must be negotiated at session setup. Any pattern is allowed if adjacent frames are no more than 256 frames apart in decoding order, which allows up to 3.41 seconds of depth at the highest ISF.

For implementers: both basic and interleaved mode SHALL be implemented. Decoding can only start at the beginning of a super-frame, and starting is RECOMMENDED only if at least 2 of its 4 transport frames are available. The RFC gives an example algorithm to recover lost-frame timestamps after an ISF change. If the payload size does not match the ToC, the receiver SHOULD discard the packet.
sections.plainLanguage: If a letter gets lost, you want to lose only a word here and there rather than a whole sentence. So the sender shuffles the order of the pieces, or sends some twice, to make gaps easy to patch.

sections.title: Media Type and SDP Parameters
sections.content:
Section 7 registers audio/AMR-WB+ in the IETF tree, only for transfer over RTP. Parameters are channels (1 or 2, default 2), interleaving (the number of frame slots in the deinterleaving buffer; if absent, interleaved mode SHALL NOT be used), int-delay (minimal buffered media time, in RTP timestamp ticks), plus ptime and maxptime. Unknown parameters MUST be ignored.

In SDP, the clock rate in a=rtpmap SHALL be 72000, and remaining parameters go in a=fmtp. In offer/answer, interleaving is symmetric, while int-delay and channels are declarative. An AMR-WB+ endpoint that also supports the payload format of RFC 3267 SHOULD declare itself AMR-WB capable, since AMR-WB is a subset of AMR-WB+.
sections.plainLanguage: Before the call starts, the two sides tell each other things like mono or stereo and how much shuffling they can handle, using a short settings line.

sections.title: Congestion and Security
sections.content:
Normal RTP congestion rules apply. AMR-WB+ can help, since a sender can change frame type or ISF to lower bandwidth, and packing more frames per payload cuts header overhead at the cost of delay and robustness.

The payload format has no built-in security, and external mechanisms such as SRTP (RFC 3711) MAY be used. To keep audio confidential, all audio data bits MUST be encrypted; the header and ToC only reveal frame types. Interleaving can weaken access control briefly after a key change, because some frames in later packets were sent under the old key, so interleaving patterns should not overlap key changes. Sender authentication needs an external mechanism, and tampering could replace audio or degrade quality. The RFC judges that the format is unlikely to be a denial-of-service threat.
sections.plainLanguage: The envelope itself has no lock. If the sound is private you must put it in a locked box, and you should be careful when you swap locks in the middle of a shuffled stream.

fields.name: ISF
fields.desc: Internal sampling frequency index for all frames; 0 for frame types 0-13.

fields.name: TFI
fields.desc: Position of the first transport frame in the super-frame, 0 to 3.

fields.name: L
fields.desc: Long (8-bit) displacement fields in interleaved mode; 0 in basic mode.

fields.name: F
fields.desc: 1 if another ToC entry follows, 0 for the last one.

fields.name: Frame Type
fields.desc: Codec frame type for this group of frames.

fields.name: #frames
fields.desc: Number of frames in the group; 0 is not allowed.

data.title: SDP session description
data.code:
m=audio 49120 RTP/AVP 99
a=rtpmap:99 AMR-WB+/72000/2
a=fmtp:99 interleaving=30; int-delay=86400
a=maxptime:100
